question.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot 1+3\cdot (-2)+2\cdot x \\  & =2x-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2x-5 & =0 \\ 2x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
